To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the outer surface of Drosophilalabial palpus with taste bristles derives mostly from a dorsal portion of the anterior compartment of labial disc, and that the inner surface, which contains the pseudotrachea, derives from the posterior compartment.
the distal portion (distiproboscis) of the Drosophila labial palpus (proboscis) consists of two domains, each expressing a different combination of basic patterning (patterning) genes.

(1) The inner surface of the distal labial palpus (pseudotrachea) is derived from the dorsal portion of the posterior compartment, and (2) The outer surface of distal proboscis (with taste bristles) is derived from dorsal portions of the posterior compartment and the dorsal portion of anterior compartment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the patterning of the labial disc, a disc with a unique combination of patterning genes.
the patterning mechanisms of the distal region of the Drosophila labial disc.
the patterning of the distal part of the Drosophila labial disc and the fate map of its derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distiproboscid portion of the labial disc is composed of the dorsal half of anterior compartment and the posterior compartment, both in the M-layer, and of the dorsal portion of the anterior compartment in the L-layer.
the distiproboscid fate map in adults and pupa is similar to the fate map in late-third-instar larva.

the distiprobosic is a composite organ consisting of a distal M-layer portion (pseudotrachea) and a more proximal L-layer portion with a dorsal and ventral half, each of which is derived from a different compartment of the labial disc proper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inner surface of labial palpus and outer surface of distipproboscis are derived from two distinct areas of the late-third-instar disc-proper, one expressing Distal-less and the other, wingless and patched.

the distiprobiscis is a composite of two distinct domains, one being the outer layer, which is a derivative of the dorsal portions of the posterior compartment, and the other, a distal portion of M-layer, which gives rise to the inner layer of the distiprociscis.

the distal tip region of the labial disc is patterned by the combined action of Distal-less and wingless, and that the outer surface of distiprocipal palpi is derived from the dorsal half of both the anterior and posterior compartment, whereas the inner surface of palpi is a derivative of the posterior compartment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the distal-most region of the labial disc proper, which is the source of the distipalpus, is a derivative of the dorsal half of both the anterior and posterior compartment, and is not a derivative of the ventral half as is the case for the distal-most regions of leg and antennal disc proper.

the distiproboscid fate map is more complex than previously thought, and that the distipalpus, which is a derivative of the M-layer, is not a simple distal appendage but a structure with a complex organization.
, unlike in other imaginal discs, the fate map of the Drosophila labial disc is not simply defined by a single patterning axis.
